text:
Anya: Quick sync — can we capture a small playbook for the Hosting/Dedicated/Private boundary? We need a checklist teams can run through before assuming a feature is cross-hosting-safe.

Kai: +1. High level constraints first: auth/credentials, observability, config translation, and runtime capabilities (batching/kv cache).

Torre: I'd add "migration safety" — how fallbacks behave if a capability isn't available in the target mode. Example: hosted supports prefix cache, private doesn't. What's the fallback?

Anya: Exactly. Proposal: a 4-step verification we can automate into a CI probe: 1) Capability discovery (api surface), 2) Auth and secret flow mapping, 3) Observability mapping (metrics/logs/span names), 4) Graceful fallback policy.

Morgan: For capability discovery: a short manifest endpoint per environment that lists supported runner features (kv_cache, continuous_batching_v2, quant_profiles). We already have a few fields in the adapter manifest but it's inconsistent across adapters.

Sean: +idea. Manifest must be stable and versioned. Add a "compatibility_level" integer so we can do cheap gating in runtime: if runtime.manifest.compatibility_level < required -> reject or route to fallback.

Kai: On auth/secret mapping: hosted has ephemeral signing keys + KMS; private might use customer KMS or HSM with different rotation semantics. Checklist item: "is there an equivalent key/secret and is rotation behavior compatible?" If not, mark as manual review.

Torre: Also call out sidecar vs in-process auth: some private deployments run a local auth proxy. Feature owners must provide an auth shim layer in the adapter or use a standard sidecar contract.

Anya: Observability: teams frequently assume token-level tracing exists. Playbook should require a mapping table: metric name -> alternative name in private, and required tags (tenant_id, model, route). If mapping missing, flag for SRE onboarding.

Morgan: Fallback semantics: document three levels — HARD_FAIL, SOFT_DEGRADE, BEST_EFFORT. Example: quantization not available -> SOFT_DEGRADE (route to higher-memory variant or degrade throughput). KV cache missing -> BEST_EFFORT (no cache). HARD_FAIL for missing auth.

Sean: We should also include rollout guidance: canary only on hosting mode that matches expected runtime (e.g., don't canary a dedicated-only optimization on hosted). If feature crosses modes, our rollout config must include per-mode flags.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for branch feature/adapter-playbook on staging (canary: 2%) :rocket:

Torre: Good catch about per-mode feature flags. Suggest a small config file schema (YAML) teams must include with a PR: fields: required_capabilities, fallback_policy, auth_mapping, observability_map, rollout_constraints. Keep it minimal.

Anya: Can we get someone to draft that schema? I'll do a first pass and put it in docs repo as "hosting-boundary-playbook.md". Want a lightweight parser so CI can run quick checks.

Morgan: I'll add a linter rule in the adapter-lint pipeline to validate the manifest and the new YAML. Can add a validator that returns a human readable failure with pointers.

Sean: One more ops note: telemetry contract must include an SLA for delayed metrics from private environments — can't assume sub-5s shipping. Make sure alerts tolerant by default.

Anya: Thanks all. Action items: Anya -> draft schema PR, Morgan -> add lint rule, Torre -> example adapter mapping for private sidecar + hosted, Kai -> design manifest versioning + compatibility_level, Sean -> doc note on telemetry SLOs. We'll reconvene after PRs land. :thumbsup:

Torre: Minor: include a compatibility test that runs a small synthetic request exercising KV cache + batching behavior. That uncovered a bug last week where private adapter returned 202 on cache miss.

Anya: Good example — include that as a sample regression test in template. OK wrapping up.
